title: Python SDK: transactional streaming events and idempotent handler ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Developers using the Python SDK for streaming chat completions are having to stitch together partial events, deduplicate overlapping tokens, and implement ad-hoc retry/ack logic to avoid duplicate side-effects (DB writes, downstream calls) when streams reconnect or the client retries. Current patterns are scattered across examples and cause subtle production bugs (duplicate analytics events, double-sends).

Goal: Provide a battery-included ergonomics layer in the Python SDK that: (1) surfaces transactional semantics for streamed partials, (2) offers idempotent handler helpers and durable ack semantics, and (3) makes telemetry for dedup/duplicate-recovery visible. The API should be easy for app developers (few lines to opt-in) while being explicit for teams needing custom behavior.

Proposal summary: Add a StreamingTransaction primitive + IdempotentHandler helper. Key features: a) server-side event IDs and sequence windows are exposed; b) SDK maintains a small durable checkpoint store interface (pluggable to Redis/SQLite/file) for last-ack and last-applied-event; c) SDK provides decorators/context-managers for idempotent side-effect handlers (with optional at-most-once vs exactly-once best-effort modes); d) built-in reconciliation that can merge overlapping partial tokens and emit a canonical finalized delta; e) retry/backoff and replay helpers for reconnects that surface conflicts to the app via explicit callbacks.

Why this approach: It keeps the server simple (server emits monotonic event_id + segment_id) while moving final application semantics to the client side where business logic lives. A small checkpoint store keeps SDK lightweight and pluggable; teams with strict requirements can provide their own durable backend.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: changing server protocol, introducing distributed consensus, or guaranteeing strong exactly-once without customer-provided durable external systems.

Deliverables: API design doc + example app using FastAPI, Redis-backed checkpointing, unit and integration tests that simulate reconnects, and a small migration guide for existing users.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a StreamingTransaction primitive with clear lifecycle methods (start, commit, abort, checkpoint)
IdempotentHandler decorator exists and prevents duplicate side-effects across reconnects in the Redis-backed example
Partial-token merging produces consistent final text identical to non-streaming batch completions in 95% of randomized tests
Telemetry: metrics emitted for duplicates_detected, replays, checkpoint_latency and surface to console tests
Integration tests simulate network flaps and verify application-level at-most-once behavior for example handlers
technical_decisions: Expose server event_id + segment_id but keep payload opaque (no protocol change needed on server until backwards-incompatible features required)
Provide a CheckpointStore abstract interface (methods: load, persist, compare_and_swap) with built-in adapters: in-memory, sqlite, redis
Idempotency model: SDK implements best-effort dedup using event_id and optional user-supplied operation keys; document limitations and failure modes
Retries: default to exponential backoff with jitter and max_retries=5, but allow caller override via StreamingTransaction kwargs
Telem: use existing SDK telemetry channel for counters and tagged spans; add new tags: stream.transaction_id, stream.replay_count
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (this ticket): API prototype + Redis example + unit tests for duplication scenarios
Phase 2 (follow-up): add sqlite adapter for local dev, add helper to export checkpoint snapshots to console, and polish docs
Edge cases: long-running sessions (>24h) require checkpoint compaction; implement TTL-based cleanup for Redis adapter
Performance: checkpoint store calls must be batched when high-throughput; optimistic CAS reduces contention; document throughput limits
Backward compatibility: keep existing stream event shapes; new API should be optional and additive
